Awarding Contracts 
28.1	
Every contract and procurement action the Government enters into must comply with:
(a)	
All applicable laws and regulations;
(b)	
All applicable Government rules, policies and procedures including, but not limited to the Conditions 
of Employment and Code of Conduct and the Financial Instructions; and
(c)	
The Government’s strategic objectives and policies including any applicable procurement strategies.
28.2	
Public officers must use objective criteria set out in the tender documents to make an award recommendation. 
The Government must only award a contract to a Bidder if the tender represents Best Value.    
28.3	
The Accounting Officer must make a contract award recommendation to Cabinet for a procurement valued 
between $100,000 and $1,000,000 on receipt of a report from the Authorised Officer.
28.4	
An evaluation panel must make a contract award recommendation to Cabinet for a procurement with a value 
of at least $1,000,000, by adhering to any procedural requirements set out in the Procurement Procedure 
Manual.

#### Bahrain Tender Board e-Tendering System

The e-Tendering System  developed by the Bahrain in cooperation with the eGovernment Authority, aims to improve the government performance, streamline the procedures pertaining to tenders and government procurement.

The e-tendering system enables purchasing entities from the government sector in its first phase to prepare the purchase order, submit tender documentations.

Also, the e-tendering system allows suppliers and contractors from the private sector to purchase tender documentations through the said system and the procedures will be completed as usual.

The second stage of the e-tendering system will be implemented which shall cover h covers the full cycle of the eTendering process - starting from submitting applications of offers, announcing tender invitations for review of the willing bidders to accepting and depositing offers submitted by bidders with confidentiality and protection.

This will later be followed by opening tenders in thorough transparency and clear evaluation of the offers, and finally announcing the awarded company, all being done online.

## The government aims to implement and operate its public projects efficiently and effectively.

The Government aims to implement and operate its public projects efficiently and effectively.

The Ministry of Finance and National Economy (MoFNE) continues to achieve and accelerate sustainable development goals and to leverage the efficiencies of the private sector in quality, optimal cost, and time for delivering major projects, goods, and services.  In this regard, MoFNE has issued a manual that includes a detailed technical and financial guide to facilitate partnerships between the public and private sectors.

It works through the Ministry of Finance and National Economy to benefit from the capabilities and expertise of the private sector in providing the best services or supplying goods at the lowest costs, in addition to alleviating the financial burdens on the state’s general budget and enhancing transparency and integrity in partnership procedures with the private sector. In this regard, the Ministry of Finance and National Economy has issued a guide to regulating partnerships between the public and private sectors.

## [Button: Legal and Financial Regulations for Drafting and Concluding Government Contracts | 26-28 May 2025 (Training Finished) ]

Objectives:

  * Provide participants with legal and technical background on government contract principles.

  * Understand how to contract for various government needs.

  * Provide an overview of contracts in general and administrative contracts specifically.

  * Learn about the procedures of contracting from choosing the method to implementation.

  * Understand contract documentation and procedural requirements.

  * Clarify the powers and obligations of government entities and the rights and duties of contractors.

  * Improve participant performance in managing, supervising, and auditing government contracts.

Contents:

  * General overview of government contracts and how to distinguish their types.

  * Methods of contracting by government entities.

  * Centralized contracting.

  * Public-private partnerships.

  * Contracting procedures.

  * Contract execution.
